nodes.name: Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
For $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, for $\uprho>1$ and integers $k,N>0$, ${\Delta}>1$, consider graph 
$G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that $\|  (\UpH_{G,k})^N\|^{1/N}_{2}=\uprho$.
Also, let $\mu$ be the Hard-core model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda\leq (1-\varepsilon){\lambda_c}(\uprho)$.

There is a constant $C={C({\Delta},\uprho,k,\varepsilon)}$ such that the mixing time of Glauber dynamics on $\mu$ 
is at most $C n\log n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.7
nodes.statement:
Let $b,\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, $\uprho> 1$, $s \geq 1$, $c>0$ and 
 the integers $k,N \geq 1, {\Delta} > 1$.

Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 


Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that 
$\|  (\UpH_{G,k})^N\|^{1/N}_{2}= \uprho$.

Assume that $\mu$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$,
is $b$-marginally bounded.


For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose  there
is a $(s,\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. 

There is a bounded number $C>1$ such that for any
$\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, the influence matrix
${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$ induced by $\mu$ satisfies 


{\small
\begin{align} 
 {\rho} \left( {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \right) &\leq 
 \frac{C}{1-(1-\varepsilon/4)^{1/s}} \enspace. 
\end{align}
}

nodes.name: Proposition 9.2
nodes.statement:
Let ${\Delta}> 1$ and $k> 0$, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda, b \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma, \lambda>0$ and $b>0$. 

Let $G=(V,E)$ be of maximum degree ${\Delta}$. Consider $\mu_G$ the Gibbs distribution on $G$ 
specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$, 
while assume that $\mu_G$ is $b$-marginally
bounded.

There are constants $C_1, C_2>0$ such that, for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and any $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, 
we have
\begin{align}
\|  {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G \|_{2}  \leq C_1+ C_2 \cdot \|  |{\mathcal{L}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}| \|_{2} \enspace.
\end{align}

nodes.name: Theorem 9.1
nodes.statement:
Let ${\Delta}> 1$ and $k> 0$, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda, b \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma, \lambda>0$ and $b>0$. 

Let $G=(V,E)$ be of maximum degree ${\Delta}$. Consider $\mu_G$ the Gibbs distribution on $G$ 
specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$, 
while assume that $\mu_G$ is $b$-marginally
bounded.

There is a constant $\widehat{C}>0$ such that, for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, 
there is an ${\mathcal{E}}_{\Lambda,k}\times {\mathcal{E}}_{\Lambda, k }$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}$ over $\mathbb{R}$, 
for which we have

\begin{align}
 {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G& =\UpD_{k} \cdot \left( {\mathcal{L}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}\circ {\mathcal{N}} \right )\cdot \UpC_{k}
+ {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k} \enspace, 
\end{align}
while for any $P,Q\in {\mathcal{E}}_{\Lambda,k}$ we also have $|{\mathcal{N}}(P,Q)|  \leq \widehat{C}$.


Recall that ${\mathcal{L}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}\circ {\mathcal{N}}$ is the Hadamard product of the two matrices. 
Matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k}$ is defined in (9.4).

nodes.name: Proposition 12.1
nodes.statement:
For $k\geq 1$, there exists a constant $\widehat{c}_0\geq 1$ such that, for any $\ell\geq 2k$
 and any ${\bf q} \in \mathbb{R}^{{\mathcal{E}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$

\begin{align}
 \upf^{s}_{{\bf q}, \ell} &\leq \widehat{c}_0 \cdot 

\upg^{s}_{{\bf q}, \ell} \enspace, 
\end{align}
where the inequality between the two vectors is entry-wise.

nodes.name: Theorem 8.4
nodes.statement:
Let ${\Delta} > 1$, $k\geq 1$ and $N>1$ be integers, $c>0$, $\uprho> 1$, $s\geq 1$, while 
let $b,\varepsilon\in (0,1)$. Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 


Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that $\|  (\UpH_{G,k})^N\|^{1/N}_{2}= \uprho$. 
Assume that $\mu$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$,
is $b$-marginally bounded. For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose that there
is a $(s,\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. 


There are constants $\ell_0> 2k$, $\widehat{x}_1\geq 1$ such that,  for $\Lambda\subset V$ and 
$\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$ with  ${\rm dist}(u,w)\geq 2k$ 
and walk $P\in {\mathcal{E}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanates from $w$, the following is true:


For $\ell\geq \ell_0$, for path $W=e_1, \ldots, e_{\ell}$ from the root of $\overline{T}=T_{\rm SAW}( {G}_{P}, u)$ 
to a copy of vertex $w$, we have
\begin{align}
\prod\nolimits_{1\leq i \leq \ell} |\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})| & \leq \widehat{x}_1 \cdot (1+\varepsilon/3)^{\ell/s} \cdot \prod\nolimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell-k} |\upalpha (e_{i})| \enspace. 
\end{align}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.7
nodes.statement:
For any $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, for ${\Delta}, {\varrho}>1$, consider graph $G=(V,E)$ 
of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that $\|  {\UpA}_G \|_{2}={\varrho}$. 
Also, let $\mu$ be the Hard-core model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda\leq (1-\varepsilon){\lambda_c}({\varrho})$.

There is a constant $C={C({\Delta}, {\varrho}, \varepsilon)}$ such that the mixing time of Glauber dynamics on $\mu$ 
is at most $C n\log n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement:
Let $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, ${\varrho} > 1$, $s\geq 1$, $\zeta>0$ and 
 the integer ${\Delta} > 1$.

 Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 

Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$
such that $\| {\UpA}_G \|_{2}={\varrho}$. Also, consider $\mu$ the Gibbs
distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$.


For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{{\varrho}}$ and $c=\frac{\zeta}{{\varrho}}$, suppose that there
is a $(s,\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. Then, for any
$\Lambda\subset V$ and any $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, the influence matrix
${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$ induced by $\mu$ satisfies 


\begin{align}
{\rho} \left( {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \right) &\leq
1+ \zeta \cdot (1-(1-\varepsilon)^{s})^{-1} \cdot ({\Delta}/{\varrho})^{1-(1/s)} \enspace.
\end{align}

nodes.name: Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement:
Let $s\geq 1$, $\delta,c >0$ and the integer ${\Delta}>1$. Also, let 
$\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$, $0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 

Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$, while let 
$\mu$ the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$.

Suppose  there is a $(s,\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. 

For any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, for any diagonal, non-negative, 
non-singular $\UpD$, such that $\UpD$ and ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_G$ are conformable for multiplication
the following is true: for any $w \in V\setminus \Lambda$,  we have 
\begin{align}
\lefteqn{
 \sum\nolimits_{u \in V\setminus \Lambda } | ( \UpD^{-1}\cdot {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_G\cdot \UpD ) (w,u) |
} \hspace{.5cm}   \\

&\leq 1+  
 \frac{c}{\UpD(w,w) } \left( \sum\nolimits_{z \in N(w)\setminus \Lambda} \UpD(z,z)+ \sum\nolimits_{\ell \geq 2} \left( \delta^{\ell-1} \sum\nolimits_{u \in V\setminus \Lambda}
\left(\UpC\cdot {\UpA}^{\ell-1}_G\right)(wz, u) 
\cdot \UpD^{s}(u,u)
\right)^{{1}/{s}} \right)

\enspace,   
\end{align}
where ${\UpA}_G$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$ and matrix $\UpC$ is defined in (7.1).

nodes.name: Theorem 1.5
nodes.statement:
For $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, $\lambda>0$, $\uprho>1$ and integers $N>0$, ${\Delta}>1$, 
consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that $\|  (\UpH_{G,k})^N\|^{1/N}_{2} =\uprho$.

Let $\mu$ be the Ising model on $G$ with external field $\lambda$ and inverse temperature $\beta\in {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}({\uprho},\varepsilon)$. 

There is a constant {$C={C({\Delta}, {\uprho}, \varepsilon)}$} such that the mixing time of Glauber dynamics 
on $\mu$ is at most $C n\log n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\varepsilon, b\in (0,1)$, $\uprho>1$ and the integers $k,N \geq 1$, ${\Delta} > 1$. 
Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$, 
$\gamma >0$ and $\lambda>0$. 


Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that  $\|  (\UpH_{G,k})^N\|^{1/N}_{2} =\uprho$.
Assume that $\mu$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters  
$(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$, is $b$-marginally bounded.


For $\delta =\frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose  the set of functions  
$\{H_d\}_{1\leq d< {\Delta}}$  specified by $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$ exhibits 
$\delta$-contraction. Then,  there exists a bounded number $\widehat{C}=\widehat{C}({\Delta}, \uprho, N, b)$ s
uch that for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, 
the influence matrix  ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$ induced by $\mu$ satisfies

\begin{align} 
\textstyle {\rho} \left( {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \right) &\leq \widehat{C} \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} \enspace.
\end{align}

nodes.name: Theorem 10.1
nodes.statement:
Let $\delta, b \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ and integers ${\Delta}, k\geq 1$. 
Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$, 
$\gamma >0$ and $\lambda>0$. 

Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ while 
assume that $\mu_G$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$,
is $b$-marginally bounded.



Suppose  the set of functions $\{ H_d\}_{1\leq d< {\Delta}}$ 
specified by $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$ exhibits $\delta$-contraction.

There are constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that, for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$,
 the influence matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$, induced by $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$, satisfies 

\begin{align}
 \|  {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \|_{2}  &\leq 
 C_1+C_2 \cdot \sum\nolimits_{\ell\geq k}  \delta^{\ell} \cdot \|  ( \UpH_{G,k})^{\ell} \|_{2}  \enspace .
\end{align}
